title: Response Quality Assessment for Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Conditional Conformal Factuality
research_question: Can conformal prediction filter unreliable sub-claims from RAG answers while retaining substantially more useful content and providing marginal or group-conditional factuality guarantees?
methodology: Conformal-RAG decomposes each generated answer into sub-claims and assigns each claim a relevance score based on query-document and claim-document cosine similarities. During calibration, GPT-4o labels claim factuality using the query, ground-truth answer, and retrieved documents, after which conformal prediction selects a relevance threshold; inference removes claims below that threshold and merges the retained claims back into a coherent response. A Mondrian conditional variant partitions calibration examples into known groups and learns a separate threshold for each group, and experiments cover FActScore, PopQA, HotpotQA, and MedLFQA using a FAISS retriever and GPT-4o generator.

key_findings.finding: Conformal-RAG provides a probabilistic factuality guarantee for the retained sub-claims under the conformal assumptions and the assumption that calibration annotations are correct.
The conditional variant uses Mondrian conformal prediction to provide separately calibrated thresholds for pre-specified query groups such as dataset or medical sub-domain.
The authors report that Conformal-RAG retains up to 60% more high-quality sub-claims than direct conformal factuality applied to the LLM while targeting the same reliability level.
At an 85% target factuality level on FActScore, Conformal-RAG removed 8.9% of claims while the Conformal-LLM baseline removed 86.8%.

Empirical factuality was generally at or above target for the marginal experiments, and conditional Conformal-RAG approximately achieved target factuality across the tested groups with less fluctuation than the Conformal-LLM baseline.
The conditional method assumes that group identity is known at inference and does not itself address arbitrary or continuously changing distribution shift.

Conformal-RAG is a post-generation claim-filtering mechanism rather than an iterative evidence-sufficiency or retrieval-budget stopping controller, and it does not track temporal document versions or source permissions.

limitations: The basic conformal guarantee relies on calibration and test examples satisfying the usual i.i.d./exchangeability condition.
The factuality guarantee assumes that the automatic calibration annotation function correctly labels factual and non-factual claims.
Conditional calibration requires the relevant group label to be available at inference time.
The experimental grouping captures known sub-domains rather than arbitrary unseen or non-stationary distribution shifts.
GPT-4o is used for calibration annotation, answer decomposition, and answer re-merging, introducing dependence on an external LLM at several stages.
Filtering low-scoring claims controls factuality but does not guarantee completeness of the remaining answer or quantify important omitted claims.
The framework does not iteratively retrieve additional evidence when a response is insufficient.
It does not represent temporal/version provenance, source supersession, or permission-aware evidence access.
raw_claims: Conformal-RAG scores each generated sub-claim using its similarity to retrieved documents weighted by query-document similarity.
Calibration uses ground-truth answers and retrieved documents to automatically label sub-claim factuality.
Inference does not require a ground-truth answer.
Claims scoring below the conformally calibrated threshold are removed.
The conditional method calibrates separate thresholds for pre-defined groups.
The experimental conditional groups are known at inference time.
The evaluation uses FActScore, PopQA, HotpotQA, and MedLFQA.
The authors test target error levels from 0.05 through 0.40.
Conformal-RAG retains substantially more claims than the Conformal-LLM baseline at matched factuality targets.
The implementation is linked through a public GitHub repository.
